judge_reasoning: The model's solution attempts to activate Mirage Mirror's own 'becomes a copy' ability sequentially after Mirror has already become a copy of Multiform Wonder. Once Mirror copies another permanent, it loses its own printed abilities (including the copy-ability itself) unless the copied permanent also has that ability, which Multiform Wonder does not. The official solution specifically works around this by activating the copy ability twice on the stack while Mirror is still 'Mirage Mirror' before either resolves, then using the Wonder-granted flying ability in between resolutions - precisely to avoid the illegal action the model performs. The model's sequential execution (resolve Wonder-copy, then try to reactivate the copy ability) is not rules-legal, so it fails to produce a 10/10 flying Colossus copy, and the remaining attackers cannot guarantee lethal damage against the opponent's blockers.
model_solution:
1. Tap 4 lands and cast Hedron Archive.
2. Cast Metalwork Colossus for {0} (noncreature artifacts: Bomat Bazaar Barge 4 + Mirage Mirror 3 + Hedron Archive 4 = 11 = full reduction).
3. Tap Hedron Archive for {C}{C} and the last 2 lands (4 mana available).
4. Pay {2}: Mirage Mirror becomes a copy of Multiform Wonder until end of turn.
5. Pay your 1 energy to Mirror's (Multiform Wonder) ability: Mirror gains flying until end of turn.
6. Pay {2}: Mirage Mirror becomes a copy of Metalwork Colossus until end of turn. It is now a 10/10 artifact creature that still has flying (the ability-granting effect from step 5 applies in layer 6, above the copy effect in layer 1, so it persists).
7. Go to combat and attack with the Mirror (10/10 flying Metalwork Colossus). It has been under your control since the start of the turn, so it isn't summoning sick. (You may also attack with Multiform Wonder and Bomat Bazaar Barge crewed by the real Colossus, but it isn't needed.)
8. The opponent's Hollow Ones and Chaos Maw have neither flying nor reach, so the Mirror cannot be blocked. It deals 10 damage – exactly lethal against 10 life.

Puzzle conventions:
Winning
Unless otherwise stated, you must win the puzzle by inflicting lethal damage to your opponent before the turn ends. This can be as late as during the cleanup step if necessary. Your solution must work for all possible outcomes, such as your opponent’s actions and blocking decisions (see below.)
Phase
Unless otherwise stated, you begin each puzzle at the beginning of your first main phase. You have already drawn a card and gone past upkeep triggers. You have not yet played a land, cast any spells, activated any abilities of permanents on the battlefield, or attacked.
Your Opponent’s Resources / Actions
Unless otherwise stated, your opponent has no cards in hand and no other permanents in play (including no lands – despite the lack of realism there.) This means the only actions you need to consider are activated abilities with no mana cost. Most puzzles with opponent actions will offer more information on this.
Blocking
You cannot assume that your opponent will block a certain way, unless they are somehow forced to. Your solution must satisfy all possible blocking scenarios, even ones that would seem strange in a regular game, and always deal lethal in order to be correct.
Dice
Sometimes you will see six-sided dice placed on cards. These are meant to indicate counters, of whatever type is most reasonable to be there. On most creatures they will be +1/+1 counters, on most artifacts and lands they will be charge counters, and on most Planeswalkers they will be loyalty counters.
If the card specifies a type of counter itself, however (like Icatian Javelineers or Raging Ravine), that will dictate which type it is. 
For -1/-1 counters, we will use a separate graphic to avoid confusion.
Zones
Unless otherwise stated, all zones not displayed are empty. Neither you nor your opponent have cards in graveyards or in exile.
Cards Drawn from Libraries
In any puzzle in which either player might draw cards or otherwise access their library, the puzzle will stipulate some known or assumed information about the library.
Most commonly, this will be a statement that you should assume that the cards remaining in libraries are to be assumed to be irrelevant to the puzzle.
Your Life
Occasionally, your own life total might appear to matter – for cards like Anguished Unmaking, for example. If we require you to consider your own life total in a puzzle, it will be displayed.
If your life total is not shown, you may assume it is irrelevant and effectively infinite.

When you are ready to answer, put your final winning line inside <solution> tags:

<solution>
1. First step...
2. Second step...
</solution>

Your line must be legal under the rules and must win against all possible opponent responses and blocking decisions.

**Key insight:** Mirage Mirror can change what it copies mid-turn, and any ability it gained while it was a copy of something else (layer 6 effect) stays on it after it becomes a copy of something new (layer 1 copy effect – rule 613.1). So we give the Mirror flying while it's a Multiform Wonder, then turn it into a 10/10 Metalwork Colossus that still flies. The Mirror has been under our control since the turn began, so it can attack.

Mana check: 6 lands. Hedron Archive (4) makes noncreature-artifact mana value 4 (Barge) + 3 (Mirror) + 4 (Archive) = 11, so Colossus costs {0}. Archive's {C}{C} plus the 2 remaining lands = 4 mana = two Mirror activations. Energy: the 1 we start with is exactly enough for one flying activation.

<solution>
1. Tap 4 lands and cast Hedron Archive.
2. Cast Metalwork Colossus for {0} (noncreature artifacts: Bomat Bazaar Barge 4 + Mirage Mirror 3 + Hedron Archive 4 = 11 = full reduction).
3. Tap Hedron Archive for {C}{C} and the last 2 lands (4 mana available).
4. Pay {2}: Mirage Mirror becomes a copy of Multiform Wonder until end of turn.
5. Pay your 1 energy to Mirror's (Multiform Wonder) ability: Mirror gains flying until end of turn.
6. Pay {2}: Mirage Mirror becomes a copy of Metalwork Colossus until end of turn. It is now a 10/10 artifact creature that still has flying (the ability-granting effect from step 5 applies in layer 6, above the copy effect in layer 1, so it persists).
7. Go to combat and attack with the Mirror (10/10 flying Metalwork Colossus). It has been under your control since the start of the turn, so it isn't summoning sick. (You may also attack with Multiform Wonder and Bomat Bazaar Barge crewed by the real Colossus, but it isn't needed.)
8. The opponent's Hollow Ones and Chaos Maw have neither flying nor reach, so the Mirror cannot be blocked. It deals 10 damage – exactly lethal against 10 life.
</solution>
